newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends at record, bonds edge higher, dollar dips.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends at record, bonds edge higher, dollar dips.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed at another record high on Monday, as Wall Street bet that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged at a policy-setting meeting next week.
Bonds, which also rallied, ended just slightly higher after a bout of profit-taking. The dollar slumped to its lowest level against the Japanese yen in almost four months.
The Dow closed up 123.22 points, or 1.72 percent, at 7,292.75, beating by a wide margin its May 6 record finish of 7,225.32.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,766 to 760 on moderate volume of about 459 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index also set an all-time high, adding 12.88 points to 837.66, and the NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 6.34 to 435.57, also a new high.
The dollar's slump to its lowest level against the Japanese yen since January also buoyed sentiment, fuelling hopes that a cheaper currency would boost the earnings of multi-national companies.

The dollar fell to 119.45 yen in late trading from 120.25 yen late Friday, after a senior Japanese government official said that last week's substantial yen gains against the dollar were not excessive. But the dollar rose to 1.7070 German marks from 1.6880 marks.

Analysts said the market was less concerned that the Fed would raise interest rates again at its next policy-setting meeting on May 20. The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point March 25 in a pre-emptive move against inflation.
"I think it's still the growing perception that the Fed is not going to raise rates," said John Church, chief investment officer at Glenmede Trust Co.
On Wednesday, the government will report on the Producer Price Index for April, and the current forecast is for a drop of 0.1 percent after another decrease of 0.1 percent in March.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury was up 2/32, leaving its yield steady at 6.89 percent.
Crude oil prices surged by almost $1.00 a barrel in New York as a series of potentially bullish international developments triggered a wave of speculative buying.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil futures for June delivery settled up 95 cents a barrel at $21.38.
June heating oil ended 2.13 cents higher at 56.65 cents a gallon while June gasoline was up 1.58 cents at 64.47 cents a gallon.

On New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, coffee for July delivery surged 11.75 cents a pound to 229.65 cents, as bullish sentiment linked to low stocks was re-ignited by a report from brokerage Merrill Lynch.

Soybean futures on the Chicago Board of Trade closed sharply lower after the Agriculture Department forecasted that the nation's farmers are set to harvest their biggest soybean crop ever and their second biggest corn crop.
Soybeans for July delivery closed down 20-1/2 cents a bushel at $8.68-1/2. July corn fell 5 cents to $2.83 a bushel.
Overseas, London's FTSE finished 38.7 points higher at 4,669.6. In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 average gained 340.73 points or 1.72 percent to close at 20,143.51.
